attributes.cardDescription: A job requisition: title, department, hiring manager, lifecycle status, headcount, salary range, and job description
attributes.readMe:
# Position

## Summary
A job requisition/opening. `jobTitle`, `department` (plain string), `status` (open | on-hold | filled | closed), `postedDate`, `targetStartDate`, `headcount`, `salaryMin`/`salaryMax`, `jobDescription`, and `hiringManager` (linksTo any Employee-shaped card). `title` is computed from `jobTitle`.

## Import
```ts
import { Position } from './position';
```

## Usage — three or more ways this is used

**1. As the requisition three other cards point at.** `Application.position`,
`Candidate.position` and `Offer.position` all link here, so the job title,
department and salary band live in exactly one place.

**2. As the salary-band source.** `salaryRangeLabel` / `salaryRangeLabelFull`
render `salaryMin`/`salaryMax` as a compact `$140k–$170k` for tiles and a full
`$140,000 – $170,000` for the detail view. Both are null-safe **and zero-safe**.

**3. As the requirement list.** `requiredSkills` is a
`linksToMany(() => Skill)`, so a Position states its bar in the same vocabulary
the resume extractor matches against.

**4. As the approval chain.** `hiringManager` owns the req; `approvalChain`
(an `ApprovalChainField` — see approval-chain-field.gts) is the sequential
sign-off gate that must reach `status: 'approved'` before hiring proceeds
through it. Replaces the old `approvers` (`linksToMany(() => Employee)`),
which recorded who COULD approve but never whether or in what order they had.

**5. As a staleness signal.** `postedDate` feeds `daysOpen()`; a req open 45+
days while still `open` is flagged as ageing — a state none of the four
hand-set statuses can express.

## Template Usage
Isolated shows the full facts grid (headcount, salary range, dates, hiring manager) plus job description. Fitted degrades from a badge (icon + status) up through a tile that adds salary range and headcount.

## Reuse notes
`department` is a plain StringField, not a `linksTo` a Team card — this keeps Position consumable by any HRIS-flavored app that has *an* Employee-like hiring manager but not necessarily this app's Team model. `hiringManager` only assumes the target satisfies the base Employee shape (name/role/department), not the specific `employee` class.

**Non-goals:** public job-posting copy/SEO fields (a separate JobPosting concept would own that); candidate sourcing/channel tracking (Application.source owns that).
